title: Learning to conduct: NYU courses while with Sarah Vaughan
summary: He wanted to be a writer and took correspondence courses at NYU while with Sarah, then moved from the piano to the podium.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: You mentioned that you had your first conducting lessons from Eubie.
How did that happen? Did you -- why did you decide to learn conducting? Was it a point in your career that you wanted to start conducting or --
-- you needed to, or was that when you were with Sarah, or --
Just a thing that I wanted to do. I always felt in my heart that I was going to be a writer. And if you're going to be a writer you have to learn how to conduct your material.

And to interpret it. And to go to school and learn how. So consequently when I was with Sarah I just took correspondence courses at NYU, to keep myself going, you know. Because they used to kid me about going -- actually we'd get off of work at night, about going home and going to bed early. Because I had homework to do.

And later on, when I did some albums with Sarah, then she found out. I told her -- we call her Sass, that's her nickname, you know. I said, 'Sass, I just had to study because I had to advance plans.' Just couldn't stay in one I

spot, you know, even though I loved the way she sang. But I couldn't -- I couldn't stay in that one spot. As I'm restless now. I can't stay in one spot now. I don't know where I'm going, but I want to go somewhere.
But you're doing a variety of things, aren't you?

Oh, yes. But that was like a major step in a particular direction. It wasn't too much variety there. It was just a -- maybe a switch over to another echelon of the industry, just to walk away from the piano and get up in front of the orchestra.
